subtitle: How a Valley King Bound a Kingdom in Writing

panels.shot: low-angle, dramatic three-quarter view of a royal hall, half in shadow, with King Loiyumba seated before an unfurled palm-leaf charter
panels.action: King Loiyumba sits upright on a carved throne in Kangla, one hand resting on a bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts spread before him, courtiers dimly visible, misty Manipur hills looming through the open hall beyond.

dialogue.text: In mist-ringed Kangleipak, King Loiyumba is said to have done what few rulers dared—bind a living kingdom into written rules.

i18n.hi: कुहरे से घिरे कांग्लेपाक में राजा लोयुम्बा ने वो किया जो कम ने किया—ज़िंदा राज्य को लिखे हुए नियमों में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over the Manipur valley, then gently descending toward Kangla fortress
panels.action: From high above, the green Manipur valley stretches like a bowl of water and fields, Kangla’s earthen walls and wooden halls at its heart, while smoke rises from clustered villages along winding streams.

dialogue.text: Eleventh-century Kangleipak was a bowl of hills and water, Meitei villages in the valley, clan chiefs in the heights, all watched from the Dragon Court of Kangla.

i18n.hi: ग्यारहवीं सदी का कांग्लेपाक पहाड़–पानी का कटोरा था—घाटी में मैतेई बस्तियाँ, ऊपर क़बीले के मुखिया, सब पर नज़र कंगला की ड्रैगन दरबार की।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a dim storehouse, lit by oil lamps, with arms, grain and tribute stacked unevenly
panels.action: King Loiyumba stands in a storeroom with officers; rows of spears, rice baskets and tribute goods lie in untidy heaps, some labeled with clan symbols, others mixed and disputed, as men gesture in confusion.

dialogue.text: Power here flowed through custom and memory. Who owed grain, spears, or soldiers was often settled by voice, not writing. Disputes rose as fast as the mist.

i18n.hi: यहाँ ताकत रिवाज़ और याददाश्त से चलती थी। किस पर अनाज, भाले या सिपाही का कर्ज़ है, ये ज़्यादातर ज़ुबान से तय होता, लिखाई से नहीं। झगड़े धुंध जितनी तेज़ उठते।

panels.shot: tight medium shot of a council scene, low-angle from floor level gazing up at seated nobles and Loiyumba
panels.action: In the council hall, Loiyumba sits attentive among clan nobles and officers, some arguing heatedly, others silent; a village headman kneels between them, clutching a staff, caught in their glare.

dialogue.text: The Cheitharol Kumbaba remembers Loiyumba amid such councils. Tradition says his court wrestled with land, labor, and tribute as the valley’s web grew tighter.

i18n.hi: चेइथारोल कुम्बाबा लोयुम्बा को ऐसे ही दरबारों के बीच याद करता है। कहा जाता है उसका दरबार ज़मीन, मज़दूरी और नज़राने पर जूझता रहा, जैसे जैसे घाटी का जाल कसा।

panels.shot: close-up on Loiyumba’s face in three-quarter profile, lamplight catching his eyes as he looks down at empty palm leaves
panels.action: Loiyumba leans over a low desk, fingers resting on blank palm leaves, his brows knit in thought while a scribe waits nearby with an iron stylus poised.

dialogue.text: Later tradition gives this moment a sharp edge: a king looking at empty leaves, asking if a realm can be held by memory alone.

i18n.hi: बाद की यादों में यही घड़ी खंजर जैसी बनती है—एक राजा खाली पत्तों को देख सोचता है, क्या राज सिर्फ़ याद पर टिक सकता है?

panels.shot: wide interior shot of the royal hall, with artisans, village heads and hill envoys arrayed in ordered rows
panels.action: The great hall is filled with carpenters, weavers, smiths, priests, valley elders and a few hill envoys, each group grouped together, while Loiyumba sits at the center, a palm-leaf bundle beside him.

dialogue.text: The Loiyumba Shinyen, a later Puya, remembers him gathering craft guilds, village heads, and hill envoys to frame their duties in words that could not be easily twisted.

i18n.hi: लोयुम्बा शिन्येन, बाद की पुया, बताती है कैसे उसने दस्तकार संघों, गाँव मुखियों और पहाड़ी दूतों को बुलाकर उनकी ड्यूटी ऐसे शब्दों में बाँधी जिन्हें आसानी से तोड़ा–मरोड़ा न जा सके।

panels.shot: side-on medium shot of a scribe’s hands incising characters onto palm leaf while Loiyumba dictates in the background
panels.action: A scribe kneels, carefully etching Meitei script into a palm leaf with a stylus, while behind him Loiyumba stands, speaking slowly, one hand raised as if measuring each phrase.

dialogue.text: The charter lists panas—administrative circles—and ties each to duties. It imagines the kingdom not as mere subjects, but as offices bound to tasks.

i18n.hi: उस सनद में पना—प्रशासनिक घेरों—की लिस्ट है, और हर एक से जुड़ी ज़िम्मेदारियाँ। वह राज्य को केवल प्रजा नहीं, कामों से बँधे दफ़्तरों की तरह सोचती है।

panels.shot: diagrammatic wide shot of the valley rendered cinematically, with subtle visual divisions showing different panas and their villages
panels.action: The valley is shown like a painted map laid before Loiyumba: circles and lines subtly mark different panas, each anchored by villages, waterways and paths reaching toward the encircling hills.

dialogue.text: In later memory, each pana owed labor and tribute. The charter fixed which households turned to fields, which to the king’s work, and when.

i18n.hi: बाद की यादों में हर पना पर मेहनत और नज़राने का कर्ज़ था। सनद ने तय कर दिया कौन–कौन से घर खेत में रहेंगे, कौन राजा की सेवा में, और कब।

panels.shot: medium shot of a group of able-bodied men being counted and assigned by an official in a village courtyard
panels.action: In a village courtyard, an official with a staff points to young men standing in line; some are marked off on a palm leaf list, older villagers watching as those chosen sling tools over their shoulders.

dialogue.text: From such lists grew the remembered lallup—rotating corvée. Men served the king in turns, then returned to their fields, their obligation inscribed rather than guessed.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं सूचियों से यादों वाला लल्लुप उगा—घूम–घूम कर होने वाली बेगार। आदमी बारी–बारी राजा की सेवा करते, फिर खेतों को लौटते, उनका फर्ज़ अब लिखित था, अनुमान नहीं।

panels.shot: interior workshop shot, with specialist artisans at work under the gaze of an official holding a palm-leaf charter
panels.action: In a bustling workshop, smiths hammer metal, clothiers work looms, and a potter shapes clay, while an official stands at the doorway holding a rolled palm-leaf charter, indicating a finished spear and shield.

dialogue.text: The Loiyumba Shinyen assigns crafts to clans and households—armorsmiths, weavers, potters—stating who must supply what for war and ritual, and when the court may call upon them.

i18n.hi: लोयुम्बा शिन्येन क़बीलों और घरों को हुनर बाँटता है—ज़िरहसाज़, बुनकर, कुम्हार—कौन युद्ध और रस्मों के लिए क्या देगा, और दरबार उन्हें कब बुला सकता है।

panels.shot: wide shot at the edge of the hills, with hill chiefs and valley envoys exchanging gifts before a backdrop of forest ridges
panels.action: On a grassy ridge where valley meets hill, Loiyumba’s envoy stands with a palm-leaf roll, while a hill chief presents forest produce and a spear; both parties gesture toward their respective lands below.

dialogue.text: The charter also speaks of hills. It remembers set tribute—forest goods, warriors, allegiance—binding upland chiefs to Kangla by negotiated duty rather than mere threat.

i18n.hi: यह सनद पहाड़ों की भी बात करती है। तयशुदा नज़राने—जंगल की चीज़ें, योद्धा, वफ़ादारी—याद रखती है, ताकि ऊपरी सरदार सिर्फ़ डर से नहीं, मोल–तय फ़र्ज़ से कंगला से बँधें।

panels.shot: close-up of an elder’s weathered hands tracing the engraved letters of the Puya by lamplight
panels.action: In a later century’s dim hut, an elder’s hands gently open a worn Puya, fingers tracing its faded etched lines, the lamplight revealing the Meitei script of the Loiyumba Shinyen.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars caution that this Puya is not an eleventh-century autograph. Its palm leaves carry memories recopied, reshaped, and read anew.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान चेताते हैं कि ये पुया ग्यारहवीं सदी की मौलिक लिखाई नहीं। इसकी ताड़–पत्तियाँ यादों की हैं, बार–बार नकल, बदली और नयी तरह से पढ़ी गयीं।

panels.shot: split-panel style wide shot: one side showing Loiyumba in his court, the other side showing later scholars around a table with texts
panels.action: On the left, Loiyumba presides over a court scene, palm-leaf bundle at his side; on the right, present-day historians lean over printed books and manuscript facsimiles, pointing to passages in discussion.

dialogue.text: Cheitharol Kumbaba, reconstructed from later copies, and works like Renuka Devi’s show how this charter sits between chronicle, memory, and administrative change.

i18n.hi: बाद की नकलों से जोड़ा गया चेइथारोल कुम्बाबा, और रेणुका देवी जैसे विद्वानों के काम दिखाते हैं कि यह सनद कैसे इबारत, याद और बदले हुए राजकाज के बीच कहीं टिकती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Loiyumba handing a rolled charter to a senior official in the hall, with officers kneeling
panels.action: Loiyumba stands from his throne and extends a rolled palm-leaf charter to a kneeling senior official, who bows deeply as other officers kneel in a semicircle behind him.

dialogue.speaker: king_loiyumba
dialogue.text: Let each know his duty before the dispute, not after it.

i18n.hi: झगड़े से पहले हर कोई अपना फर्ज़ जान ले, बाद में नहीं।

panels.shot: wide village scene showing lallup service and home life side by side
panels.action: In one half of the frame, men labor repairing a road and fortress wall under an overseer holding a charter; in the other, the same men later work in their flooded paddy fields with families watching.

dialogue.text: Under later Ningthou kings, lallup and panas became the bones of Manipur’s state. Whatever their precise birth, Loiyumba’s name stayed tied to this web of written duty.

i18n.hi: आगे के निंगथौ राजाओं के समय लल्लुप और पना मणिपुर के राज–ढाँचे की हड्डियाँ बन गए। जन्म जैसा भी रहा हो, लिखित फ़र्ज़ के इस जाल से लोयुम्बा का नाम जुड़ा ही रहा।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from the floor of the court, looking up past stacked Puyas toward Loiyumba framed against the open sky
panels.action: Stacks of palm-leaf Puyas rise in the foreground, silhouetted, while beyond them Loiyumba stands at the edge of the open hall, looking out toward the valley and hills under a wide, cloud-scattered sky.

dialogue.text: In Meitei memory, Loiyumba stands at the threshold where a ruler’s word begins to share space with written office—where power is not only commanded, but carefully inscribed.

i18n.hi: मैतेई याद में लोयुम्बा उस देहरी पर खड़ा है जहाँ राजा की ज़ुबान पहली बार लिखित ओहदों से जगह बाँटती है—जहाँ ताकत सिर्फ़ हुक्म नहीं, नाप–तौल कर लिखी जाती है।

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot of a present-day Manipur landscape with faint superimposed ghostly outline of Loiyumba’s court
panels.action: A contemporary view of the Manipur valley, roads and houses scattered across the plains, while faint, translucent lines suggest the ghostly outline of Loiyumba’s hall and charter floating over the land.

dialogue.text: His story asks us to see law not as distant parchment, but as a living bargain between land, labor, and ruler—one that each age must choose to rewrite or remember.

i18n.hi: उसकी कहानी हमें कानून को दूर की चिट्ठी नहीं, ज़मीन, मज़दूरी और राजा के बीच जिंदा सौदा मानने को कहती है—जिसे हर दौर या तो फिर से लिखता है, या सँभाल कर याद रखता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Valley King Bound a Kingdom in Writing
subtitle_i18n.hi: घाटी के राजा ने लिखकर कैसे बाँधा अपना राज्य
